name: Pictory
tagline: Create and repurpose videos from scripts, articles and long recordings.
shortDescription: AI video tool for turning scripts and articles into videos and repurposing long recordings into short clips.
description: Pictory is a browser-based AI video tool. It helps create videos from scripts or articles and can be used to repurpose longer recordings into shorter clips.
It is aimed at marketers, educators and creators who want to produce video regularly without a traditional editing workflow.
Pictory has offered a free trial rather than a permanent free plan; check the official website for current trial terms and plan limits.

pricing.notes: Demo profile: plan names and prices have not been recorded yet. Check the official website for current pricing.

keyFeatures.title: Script and article to video
keyFeatures.description: Builds a video from written content by matching text with visuals.

keyFeatures.title: Repurpose long videos
keyFeatures.description: Helps create shorter clips from longer recordings such as webinars.

keyFeatures.title: Captions
keyFeatures.description: Adds captions to videos. Check the official site for supported languages.

howItWorks: Start a trial or plan on the official website.
Choose to start from a script, an article URL or an existing video.
Review the scenes, visuals and captions it suggests.
Adjust, add a voiceover or music, and export.
pros: Designed for repurposing content you already have
cons: Free access is via a trial — check current terms
Automatically chosen visuals usually need manual review

checklist: Relevance of automatically matched visuals for a 600-word article
Caption accuracy on a recording with clear speech
Trial length and limits on the date of testing
Export resolution available on the entry-level plan

faqs.a: Pictory has offered a free trial. Check the official pricing page for current trial terms and plan details.

faqs.q: What is the difference between Pictory and Fliki?
faqs.a: Both create videos from text. See our Fliki vs Pictory comparison for a detailed look at how they differ and which type of user each suits.
